title: Immunoaffinity purification of endogenous proteins from S. cerevisiae for post-translational modification and protein interaction analysis
protocol: Grow yeast cultures expressing FLAG-tagged protein in YPD medium.
Inoculate 20 mL of YPD medium with a single colony and grow at 30°C for 16–18 hours.
Measure the optical density (OD600) of the yeast culture using a spectrophotometer.
Dilute the culture to an OD600 = 0.2 in 2 L of sterile YPD medium.
Grow the diluted culture at 30°C until cells reach an OD600 ∼1.0 (5–6 hours).
Harvest cells by centrifugation in 500 mL bottles at 4300 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Pour off supernatant and wash pellet with ice-cold sterile, deionized water.
Resuspend the pellet in 40 mL of ice-cold sterile, deionized water and transfer to a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 2850 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Pour off supernatant.
Resuspend cells in a volume of lysis buffer equivalent to the size of the pellet.
Add the cell suspension drop-wise into liquid nitrogen using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Collect the yeast suspension beads from the liquid nitrogen using a metal strainer or pipette tip rack insert.
Transfer the collected yeast suspension beads to a 50 mL conical tube.
Store the conical tube containing the yeast suspension beads at -80°C.
Fill a pre-chilled coffee grinder with small pellets of dry ice.
Add yeast suspension beads to the coffee grinder containing dry ice.
Grind the mixture for 1 min until it forms a fine powder.
Pour/scrape the ground cells into a 14 ml polypropylene centrifuge tube.
Place the tube on ice and allow the dry ice to evaporate.
Add 1 mM PMSF and 1× EZBlock Protease Inhibitor Cocktail IV (diluted from the stock) to the lysate.
Add 1× PhosSTOP phosphatase inhibitor to the lysate following commercial vendor recommendations.
Add NP-40 to a final concentration of 0.4% in the lysate and invert 10 times to mix well.
Reconstitute a 10× stock solution of PhosSTOP phosphatase inhibitors by dissolving one tablet in 1 mL of deionized water.
Store the prepared PhosSTOP stock at 4°C for up to 1 month or -20°C for up to 6 months.
Alternatively, directly dissolve the PhosSTOP tablet into the lysate.
Cut a PhosSTOP tablet on parafilm and add smaller pieces to the lysate to speed dissolution.
Sonicate lysates three times for 30 seconds each at 15% output with at least one minute on ice between rounds if necessary.
Clarify the lysate by centrifugation at 3094 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Pipette 75 μL of bead slurry per IP into a microfuge tube (for two IPs, use 150 μL).
Add 1 mL of yeast lysis buffer to the tube and mix by inverting 5-6 times.
Place the tube on a magnetic stand and allow beads to collect against the wall of the tube.
Remove supernatant and repeat wash with 1 mL of lysis buffer, mixing by inversion.
Place the tube back on the magnetic stand and remove supernatant after beads have collected.
Resuspend beads in a bead-equivalent volume of lysis buffer to generate a 50/50 slurry.
Use wide-bore, low-retention tips when pipetting beads.
Do not vortex beads; use gentle inversion or a rotator for resuspending beads.
Transfer the supernatant to a 15 mL conical tube and place clarified lysate on ice in an ice bucket.
Determine the protein concentration of the lysate using a Bradford assay.
Add 1 mL of Bradford reagent to disposable cuvettes for each protein sample including a blank control.
Add 1 μL of lysate to the cuvette, cover the top with a small piece of parafilm, and invert the cuvettes 4–6 times to mix the solution well.
Incubate the cuvettes at 25°C for 10 min.
Measure the absorbance at 595 nm for each sample using a visible light spectrophotometer.
Develop a standard curve using BSA or other protein of known quantity.
Measure absorbance in yeast lysis buffer for the standard curve ranging from 4 mg/mL to 40 mg/mL.
Normalize protein concentration for tagged and untagged protein lysate.
Remove 100 μL from the lysate as a total lysate sample for future western blot analysis.
Add 25 μL of 5× SDS sample buffer to the lysate sample, boil for 5 min, and store at -20°C.
Mix washed FLAG magnetic beads with normalized lysate in 15 mL conical tubes.
Rotate samples on a tube rotator at 8 rpm for 3 hours at 4°C.
Place tubes in a magnetic stand after incubation to allow the beads to collect.
Remove supernatant by pipetting and save a 100 μL aliquot for western blot analysis.
Wash the beads 3 times with yeast lysis buffer.
Add 5 mL of cold yeast lysis buffer to the beads.
Rotate for 5 min at 4°C.
Place the tubes in the magnetic stand and remove the supernatant once beads collect.
Repeat the wash with 5 mL of yeast lysis buffer.
Repeat the wash using 5 mL of yeast lysis buffer supplemented with 0.5% NP-40.
Transfer the beads to a new microfuge tube using 500 μL of yeast lysis buffer + 0.5% NP-40.
Wash the old tube and pipette tip with an additional 500 μL of buffer.
Add the buffer and any more beads collected to the new tube.
Place the tubes in the magnetic stand, allow the beads to collect, and remove the supernatant.
Use wide-bore, low-retention tips to completely collect all beads and transfer to a new tube.
Prepare elution buffer by adding 0.2 mg/mL 3xFLAG peptide to yeast lysis buffer.
Add 50 μL of FLAG elution buffer to the tube with FLAG magnetic beads from Step 13.
Rotate the samples on a tube rotator at 8 rpm for 30 min at 4°C.
Place the tubes in the magnetic stand and allow the beads to collect on the side of the tube.
Carefully transfer the supernatant to a new tube, avoiding disturbing the beads.
Perform a second elution by adding 50 μL of FLAG elution buffer to the beads.
Rotate at 4°C for 30 min.
Place the tubes in the magnetic stand.
Allow the beads to collect on the side of the tube.
Carefully transfer the supernatant to a new tube, avoiding disturbing the beads.
Remove 15 μL of Eluate #1 and #2 into new tubes.
Add 3.8 μL of 5× SDS sample buffer to each removed eluate.
Boil for 5 min.
Store at −20°C for use in SDS-PAGE followed by silver stain or western blotting.
Freeze the remaining sample in liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen sample at −80°C until mass spectrometry is performed.
Set up the glass plates and casting apparatus for pouring the polyacrylamide gel based on the manufacturer’s instructions.
Prepare an 8% resolving gel mixture in a 15 mL conical tube.
Pour the resolving gel mixture between the glass plates, leaving approximately 3 cm space below the top of the short glass plate.
Carefully pour a layer of isopropanol over the top of the resolving gel to level out the top.
Let the resolving gel stand for 20–30 minutes until it polymerizes.
Once the resolving gel has polymerized, remove the isopropanol layer by pouring.
Perform a quick wash with 1 mL of deionized water to remove any residual isopropanol.
Use a pipette to add the stacking gel mixture on top of the resolving gel between the glass plates.
Add enough stacking gel mixture to completely fill the gap between the plates.
Place a 10-well comb between the plates.
Allow the gel to polymerize for approximately 20 minutes.
Store the gel in a damp paper towel wrapped in plastic wrap, sealed completely at 4°C for up to one week if not used immediately.
Assemble the gel electrophoresis unit and place it in the buffer tank.
Dilute the 10× SDS running buffer with deionized water to make 1 liter of 1× SDS running buffer.
Pour buffer into the chamber until the wells are covered, following the manufacturer's level indication.
Load 18 μL of IP samples in SDS sample buffer and 3 μL of molecular weight marker into the gel.
Attach the gel box to the power supply.
Run the gel at a constant 200 V for approximately 45 minutes or until the dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.
Remove the gel from the running apparatus carefully.
Open the glass plates of the gel carefully.
Trim off the stacking gel using a plastic spatula, and remove excess gel outside the lanes if desired.
Place the gel in a clean staining box.
Rinse the gel briefly with deionized water.
Follow the steps for silver staining as described in the SilverQuest™ Silver Staining Kit protocol.
Wash the gel several times in deionized water after the staining procedure.
Image the gel on a white light imaging platform or dry and store it for future reference.
Prepare samples for mass spectrometry following protocols relevant to available facilities and instrumentation once elution of the target protein is confirmed by SDS-PAGE.

Choose conditions for protein digestion and other steps required prior to mass spectrometry based on the goal of identifying phosphosites, post-translational modifications, or protein interaction partners.
